biography.plain_text: Godfrey Herbert Joseph Williams was a Welsh landowner and colliery proprietor who inherited the Aberpergwm family's substantial coal and estate interests. The eldest son of Morgan Stuart Williams, he was educated at Eton and later lived in Jersey. He sold St Donat's Castle, which his father had acquired, in 1922.

long_biography.plain_text:
Godfrey Williams's visits to New Zealand left a practical legacy in the Landsborough Valley. At the end of a hunting trip in 1928, the Welsh landowner provided money for a hut on the valley flats. Con Hodgkinson and Mark Te Koiti built the shelter below Strutts Bluff; it became known as Con's Castle.

He also placed a substantial body of family papers in the National Library of Wales in 1939. The deposit included colliery accounts, diaries and correspondence, alongside letters to the folk-song collector Maria Jane Williams and Welsh and English verses she had collected. It preserved both the business records and the literary interests of the Aberpergwm household.
